text:
Mia Nguyen: FYI I finished a first-pass onboarding run for sable-32k-int3 this morning. it's an aggressive quant experiment (int3 channelwise) and i'm seeing a repeatable token alignment delta starting near 29.4k during multi-shard prefill. filing notes here.
Samir Patel: int3! nice. what's the exact runner command and flags?
Mia Nguyen: ran: 
```
./ci/longctx_onboard --model sable-32k --quant int3-channelwise --ropescale rescale2 --prefill_stride 64 --shards 4 --capture-kv --kv-checksum 256 --job sable-20260420-01
```
Mia Nguyen: quick log excerpt where things diverge:
```
[2026-04-20T06:22:12Z] KV-TILE: tile=28 start=28672 len=1024 checksum=0xd3a9b2
[2026-04-20T06:22:12Z] KV-DEQ: tile=28 checksum=0xd3a9b2
[2026-04-20T06:22:12Z] KV-TILE: tile=29 checksum=0x6e4f11
[2026-04-20T06:22:12Z] DIFF first-mismatch tile=29 offset=88 global-token=28760
[2026-04-20T06:22:12Z] INFER(INT3): token=28761 -> "agreement" prob=0.62
[2026-04-20T06:22:12Z] INFER(FP16): token=28761 -> "agreement." prob=0.93
```
Nadia H: offset 88 inside the tile, that's not just boundary jitter. did you try varying prefill_stride or kv-align?
Mia Nguyen: tried stride 64->128 and kv-align=true. stride change moved mismatch earlier by ~40 tokens; kv-align reduced frequency but didn't eliminate it.
Felix O: int3 is low-bit; rounding noise can cascade. did you attempt per-shard vs global quant scales?
Mia Nguyen: default is per-shard. i re-ran with `--quant-scale-mode global` and also toggled a new runtime option `--rotary-stabilize true` (a patch that forces consistent interpolation across quantized blocks). job sable-20260420-02.
ci-bot: job sable-20260420-01 artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-ci/sable-20260420-01/logs.tar.gz
Mia Nguyen: re-run brief results: global-scale + rotary-stabilize dropped checksum diffs from 7/10 -> 1/10. tail p95 increased ~6%. artifacts for run 02 at s3://redwood-ci/sable-20260420-02/
Samir Patel: good sign. can you localize whether the last residual failure is a numeric rounding cascade or an infra ordering issue? add rolling checksum at 128 tokens to see first mismatch tile and layer if possible.
Mia Nguyen: added rolling 128-tile checksums and a lightweight layer-mask logger. run sable-20260420-03 shows the residual mismatch maps to layer 18 accumulation and first-mismatch at 128-tile boundary offset 12.
Nadia H: layer 18 is mid-transformer. that suggests quant rounding accumulation across FFN/attn ops. Alex's prior rotary-interpolate fixed some int8 cases but int3 may need stronger dampening.
Felix O: possible mitigations: (1) use global-scale with per-layer minimal smoothing, (2) apply a tiny bias-correction on dequant at shard join, or (3) keep per-shard for low-latency profiles and fall back to global-scale for canary/dedicated onboarding.
Samir Patel: propose experiment matrix: run A: global-scale + rotary-stabilize; run B: per-shard + dequant-join-verify (materialize fp16 on join but keep shard scaling); run C: hybrid quant (layers 0..16 fp16, rest int3) to see if mismatch onset changes.
Mia Nguyen: scheduling those: sable-20260420-04 (A), sable-20260420-05 (B), sable-20260420-06 (C). ci-bot queued them.
ci-bot: job sable-20260420-02 completed, artifacts uploaded. job 04/05/06 queued.
Mia Nguyen: quick interim: run A (global-scale + rotary-stabilize) eliminated mismatches in 9/10 runs; run B (dequant-join-verify) eliminated mismatches in 8/10 while preserving ~3% lower latency vs A; run C (hybrid) moved mismatch onset much later but didn't remove it entirely.
Nadia H: sounds like dequant-join-verify is a promising middle ground. can you capture per-layer float deltas at the join op when it occurs? that will tell us whether the discrepancy is introduced pre- or post-join.
Mia Nguyen: added a tiny instrumentation that computes per-layer L2 norm between fp16 reference and dequantized int3 at join boundaries. in the failing run metric we saw a spike at layer 18 L2=0.034 versus baseline 0.001.
Samir Patel: that's convincing for quant rounding cascade. next steps: (1) add a regression test to onboarding that runs the sanitized long-legal prompt with kv-checksum=256 for 10 runs and requires <=1 mismatch; (2) add ML ticket ML-9810 to track dequant-join-verify as the recommended runtime mitigation for int3 channels; (3) measure perf impact for hosted canary vs dedicated.
Mia Nguyen: creating ML-9810 and opening PR with the rotary-stabilize guard and dequant-verify option: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/889. PR includes unit tests and CI harness changes.
ci-bot: PR runtime/pull/889 CI passed. artifacts from instrumented runs uploaded.
Felix O: couple of product notes: int3 is attractive for cost but we must document expected perf/quality tradeoffs. recommend adding a short section to the onboarding doc that explains when to prefer int3 vs int8 and the runtime flags (quant-scale-mode, rotary-stabilize, dequant-join-verify).
Mia Nguyen: will draft onboarding note and add the 29-30k tiled regression case to the onboarding checklist. scheduling a canary run of global-scale + dequant-verify on the dedicated pool to monitor tail latency for a week.
Samir Patel: once canary completes, we'll decide default runtime flags for hosted "low-latency" vs dedicated "correctness" profiles. ping me on ML-9810 for rollout plan.
Mia Nguyen: thanks all. closing thread until the canary completes. :rocket:
